one_liner: Clay has a REST Public API (api.clay.com/public/v0) with self-serve API keys on all plans including Free, plus a vendor-hosted OAuth MCP server at api.clay.com/v3/mcp.
auth_notes: The Public API uses a per-user clay-api-key header, with keys created in the Clay UI or CLI. OAuth is documented only for the hosted MCP server, not for the REST API, so OAUTH2 is left out of the REST auth methods. Keys are tied to a user, so multi-user toolkits need each user to supply their own key.
access_notes: The developer platform (API, CLI, plugin) is on every plan including Free. The Free plan caps API search at 100 results per 30 days. Tables are read-only and Enterprise-gated for structured queries. Table webhooks and the HTTP API column need Growth.
blocker_notes: The Free search cap is small. The API cannot write tables; inbound webhooks do that and need Growth. Workflows are alpha/beta. The API is new (GA Sept 2026), so stability is unproven. Details come mainly from a third-party vendor blog plus Clay-hosted pages.

evidence.quote: Create one in Clay under **API and CLI > API keys**, or run `clay api-keys create` in the CLI. Send it on every request in the `clay-api-key` header.
